questions.prompt: Clinically, how does he distinguish 'not having a life' from depression?
choices: A They are always the same diagnosis.
B A multi-dimensional check (relationships, friends, meaning, etc.) can show misery from lacking a life vs clinical depression.
C Only blood tests define either condition.
D If you have a job you cannot be either.
questions.explain: Assess whether someone has intimacy, family, friends, meaningful engagement—if not, misery may be absence of a life, not depression per se.

questions.prompt: What does he say is the right question instead of 'Where is the perfect partner for me'?
choices: A How can I lower my standards to zero?
B How can I become the person who would attract the person I would want to be with?
C How can I force someone to be right for me?
D Why bother with relationships at all?
questions.explain: The productive question is how to become the person who would attract the partner you'd want.

questions.prompt: What rule of thumb does he give for real friends regarding good and bad news?
choices: A Friends should always trump your news with their own.
B You can tell them good news and they're happy for you; you can tell bad news and they sustain you without competing misery.
C Friends exist only for networking.
D Never share news with anyone.
questions.explain: Good friends rejoice at your good news (without substituting their own 'greater' story) and support you through bad news.

questions.prompt: What does Carl Rogers establish as a cardinal rule before clinical help works?
choices: A The therapist must force insight with shock.
B The person must come wanting to be better—court-mandated unwilling clients often can't be helped that way.
C Only medication matters.
D Clients should never decide anything.
questions.explain: Rogers: the person has to come deciding they'd rather be better; forced clients may refuse that decision.

questions.prompt: In the closing recapitulation, what is the vision he asks you to build?
choices: A vague Caribbean vacation poster from age 13, left unexamined.
B How you would set the world straight optimally around yourself—decomposed into relationships, work, and concrete plans you take seriously.
C A list of people to resent.
D Only financial KPIs with no human domain.
questions.explain: Vision = optimally setting the world straight around you; decompose into relationships and actionable elements—take yourself seriously.
